JP.nov: Autumn foliage and cool city walks shape November trips across much of Japan. Kyoto can be busy near peak colour; northern and mountain areas are colder.
JP.dec: Winter illuminations and the opening ski season become travel themes. Snow and temperatures vary by region. Year-end holidays bring busy travel and some business closures.

TH.nov: Cooler, generally drier weather supports northern cultural trips and Andaman coast holidays. The Gulf islands have a different rainfall pattern and can still be very wet.
TH.dec: Inland Thailand remains in its popular cool season, with cooler mountain nights. Andaman beach travel is in season; Gulf-coast rainfall still requires checking local conditions.

AU.nov: November is spring across temperate Australia, suitable for varied outdoor itineraries. Tropical northern regions enter their wet season, so a nationwide beach-weather assumption would mislead.
AU.dec: Summer begins in the temperate south, supporting coastal and outdoor trips. The tropical north remains in its wet season; regional conditions matter more than a national average.

NZ.nov: Late spring offers nature-focused itineraries before summer. Match outdoor plans to local conditions and allow flexibility; New Zealand's mountains and coasts do not share one climate.
NZ.dec: December starts summer, when beaches and outdoor experiences feature strongly. The tourism board identifies December to February as the summer season; this is seasonal guidance, not measured demand.

AE.nov: Dubai's cooler-season calendar supports beach visits, desert excursions and outdoor dining. This regional example does not describe every emirate or establish a ranking of visitor origins.
AE.dec: Outdoor attractions, festive markets and year-end celebrations are central Dubai themes. Pleasant winter conditions support open-air itineraries; event dates and individual programmes still need separate confirmation.

QA.nov: Qatar's winter season starts in November, bringing milder conditions for souq visits, parks, waterfront walks and desert activities. These are general seasonal conditions rather than a forecast.
QA.dec: Mild daytime weather and cooler evenings favour outdoor cultural and coastal experiences. Pack for changing evening temperatures and check short-term conditions before desert or sea excursions.

ZA.nov: Cape Town moves from spring toward its sunny summer, with outdoor and food events. South Africa's regional climates differ, so safari and coastal itineraries need separate planning.
ZA.dec: Cape Town's warm summer supports beaches, gardens and outdoor performances. December is a popular visiting period there; other regions have different rainfall patterns and travel conditions.

IN.nov: Delhi's autumn generally supports sightseeing with lighter layers than midwinter. Diwali and Rajasthan's fairs add cultural interest in 2026. Conditions vary widely across India's regions.
IN.dec: Northern cities become cooler while Himalayan destinations can face snow and access constraints. Delhi and Himachal illustrate different winter experiences; a single national weather label is inappropriate.

DE.nov: Late November brings the opening of many Christmas markets. Berlin illustrates the shift toward illuminated squares, seasonal shopping and cultural city breaks; openings differ by venue.
DE.dec: Christmas markets, light displays and performances shape urban itineraries. Check each market's operating days and closing date, especially near Christmas, rather than assuming uninterrupted daily opening.

AT.nov: Many Austrian Christmas markets start during the second half of November. Alpine ski openings begin selectively, with operating dates dependent on snow, altitude and resort decisions.
AT.dec: Advent markets and skiing are complementary travel themes. Most resorts target late-November to mid-December openings, but planned dates remain conditional on weather and snow conditions.

FI.nov: Christmas markets begin to add seasonal interest, while Lapland's Santa experiences operate beyond Christmas itself. Build itineraries around local opening schedules and actual winter conditions.
FI.dec: Christmas traditions, sauna and winter outdoor activities shape trips. Rovaniemi offers Santa experiences; snow-based activities should be checked locally because conditions and availability vary by place.

NO.nov: Northern Norway moves toward polar night from mid-November. Long dark evenings suit aurora watching when skies permit, while daylight and winter conditions differ greatly by latitude.
NO.dec: Short days and northern polar night define many winter itineraries. Aurora sightings depend on conditions; choose activities and transport for the specific destination, rather than expecting guaranteed lights.

ES.nov: Autumn food, forests and rural trips feature in Spain's monthly travel guidance. Extremadura's Ambroz valley is one example, while Christmas lights begin arriving toward month end.
ES.dec: City lights, nativity scenes and Christmas markets become prominent. Madrid's New Year's Eve grape tradition is a seasonal highlight; the Canary Islands offer a different winter setting.

IT.nov: Autumn itineraries emphasise villages, countryside and regional food. Alba's truffle fair adds a dated 2026 attraction; foliage and harvest experiences depend on region and timing.
IT.dec: Christmas-decorated cities, markets and mountain holidays shape winter trips. Italy's national tourism board highlights places from Bolzano to Rome; ski conditions need separate local checks.

SG.nov: Singapore stays warm and humid. November's inter-monsoon period often brings afternoon or evening thunderstorms, so combine outdoor neighbourhood walks with flexible indoor options and rain breaks.
SG.dec: The Northeast Monsoon's wet phase can bring extended rain spells. Festive city experiences remain possible, but outdoor schedules should be flexible; climate normals are not a daily forecast.

MA.nov: Autumn is highlighted by Morocco's tourism board for Sahara trips. Coastal, inland and mountain conditions differ, so avoid applying a Marrakech or desert description to the whole country.
MA.dec: Coasts can be comparatively mild while mountain winters are cold and wet. Plan clothing and transport around altitude and route, with local checks for mountain access and conditions.

VN.nov: Vietnam needs regional planning rather than a single national season. Central-coast rain can affect itineraries; consult local conditions when combining northern, central and southern destinations.
VN.dec: The national tourism guide highlights Phu Quoc for tropical beach trips. Northern Vietnam is cooler, while central destinations can remain wet; choose regions to match the desired experience.

CA.nov: Holiday lights brighten cities as the season turns toward winter. Ontario's urban and regional routes offer one example; Canada-wide conditions vary substantially, especially for snow-dependent activities.
CA.dec: Winter city breaks can combine lights, cultural attractions and nearby snow activities. Ontario's tourism guidance stresses planning for winter driving and checking opening schedules and local conditions.

PT.nov: Portugal starts its transition into festive travel, with Óbidos's 2026 Christmas village opening in late November. Other towns run different schedules, so verify the chosen local programme.
PT.dec: Christmas traditions, seasonal food and markets shape city visits. Madeira's official 2026 programme begins December 1 and continues into January, culminating in New Year's Eve celebrations.

FR.nov: Paris's festive lights and shop windows begin appearing from mid-November. This city example supports cultural and shopping itineraries; other French regions have distinct seasonal programmes.
FR.dec: Christmas markets, illuminations, concerts and museum visits anchor Paris trips. Lyon's light festival adds a separate regional highlight; check opening hours around holidays and specific event dates.

methodology.events: Primary-source curated events, plus date-holidays calculated calendars. A holiday is not a forecast of demand. Local and regional events are not exhaustive.
methodology.flows: Only the historical annual market records shown are verified. No country has a measured November/December 2026 ranking in this dataset. Nationality, residence, visits and trips differ; read each record’s note.
methodology.coverage: 250 country and territory records, including dependencies and disputed/reference areas. Polygon source is Natural Earth 1:50m. Small places also have centroid markers and are always available through search.
methodology.crawl: Travel-guide pages are automatically fetched and indexed. They provide background reading, not independently verified forecasts. Counted pages are distinct successfully retrieved URLs, not distinct websites.
methodology.seasonal: Seasonal notes describe broad patterns, not real-time conditions, booking volume or entry guidance.
methodology.license: Wikivoyage excerpts: CC BY-SA 4.0, attributed to linked page contributors. World geography: Natural Earth public domain; country metadata: mledoze/countries (ODbL); calendars: date-holidays (ISC).
